topic: Cement (composition, manufacture, hydration, types, testing), aggregates (classification, grading, properties), and water for concrete
source: 601-80.json, 681-760.json, 761-842.json, Concrete_1-50.json, Concrete_101-150.json, Concrete_151-200.json, Concrete_50-100.json, conc_201-250.json, conc_250-300.json, conc_301-350.json, conc_350-405.json

questions.q: 1. The commonly used material in the manufacture of cement is
questions.explain: Lime stone (calcareous material) supplies the required lime (CaO) content, which forms the major ingredient of cement, hence it is the commonly used raw material.

questions.q: 2. To obtain cement dry powder, lime stones and shales or their slurry, is burnt in a rotary kiln at a temperature between
questions.explain: In the rotary kiln, the raw mix is burnt at 1400°C–1500°C, the clinkering temperature, at which the raw materials fuse to form cement clinker.

questions.q: 3. How much cement contained in one bag
questions.explain: A standard bag of cement weighs 50 kg, which corresponds to a weight (force) of about 500 N (50 × 9.81 ≈ 490.5 N ≈ 500 N).

questions.q: 4. The maximum quantity of ingredients present in cement production is
questions.explain: Lime (CaO) forms the largest proportion (about 60-65%) of the chemical composition of cement, hence it is present in maximum quantity.

questions.q: 5. The minimum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is
questions.explain: Iron oxide is present in the smallest percentage (about 3-4%) among the major ingredients (lime, silica, alumina, iron oxide) of cement.

questions.q: 6. The minimum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is that of
questions.explain: Magnesium oxide is a minor constituent and is present in the least percentage (about 1-3%) among all chemical ingredients of cement; its excess makes cement unsound.

questions.q: 7. Pick up the correct proportions of chemical ingredients of cement
questions.explain: The typical proportion of ingredients in cement is Lime 63%, Silica 22%, Alumina 6%, and Iron oxide 3%.

questions.q: 8. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: lime in excess, causes the cement to expand and disintegrate
silica in excess, causes the cement to set slowly
alumina in excess, reduces the strength of the cement
magnesium oxide in excess, remains in free state and makes the cement unsound
questions.explain: All the listed effects of excess lime, silica, alumina, and magnesium oxide are correct statements regarding their influence on cement properties.

questions.q: 9. Efflorescence in cement is caused due to an excess of
questions.explain: Excess alkalis in cement react with atmospheric moisture and carbon dioxide, forming soluble salts that migrate to the surface, causing efflorescence (white deposits).

questions.q: 10. An ordinary Portland cement when tested for its fineness, should not leave any residue on I.S sieve No 9 more than
questions.explain: As per IS specifications, the residue retained on IS sieve No. 9 (90 micron) should not exceed 10% for ordinary Portland cement, ensuring adequate fineness.

questions.q: 11. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following :
options: gypsum in cement decreases the setting time
the first compound of cement which reacts with water, is C2S
bulking of sand is less when its particles are fine
questions.explain: All three statements are actually incorrect: gypsum increases (not decreases) setting time, C3A (not C2S) reacts first with water, and bulking of sand is more (not less) when particles are fine. Hence 'all of the above' is the correct choice for incorrect statements.

questions.q: 12. Cement used for normal concrete construction, is obtained by burning a mixture of
questions.explain: Ordinary Portland cement is manufactured by burning a mixture of silicious, argillaceous (clayey), and calcareous (limestone) materials together.

questions.q: 13. The mixture of different ingredients of cement, is burnt at
questions.explain: The raw mixture of cement ingredients is burnt at approximately 1400°C, the clinkering temperature, to form cement clinker.

questions.q: 14. The cement whose strength is little lower than the ordinary cement during the first three months but attains afterwards the same strength, is known as
questions.explain: Low-heat Portland cement develops strength slowly at early stages due to lower C3S and C3A content, but eventually catches up with the strength of ordinary cement after about three months.

questions.q: 15. For construction of structures in sea water, the cement generally preferred to, is
questions.explain: Portland pozzolana cement is preferred in sea water construction as it has better resistance to sulphate attack and lower permeability, reducing chemical attack from sea water.

questions.q: 16. For quality control of portland cement, the test essentially done is
questions.explain: Quality control of Portland cement requires testing setting time, soundness, tensile/compressive strength, and consistency, hence all of these are essential.

questions.q: 17. Sieve analysis of portland cement is performed on IS sieve No.
questions.explain: Fineness of Portland cement is tested by sieving on IS Sieve No. 9 (90 micron sieve) as per Indian Standard specifications.

questions.q: 18. During manufacturing process of portland cement, gypsum or plaster of paris is added
options: to increase the strength of cement
to modify the colour of cement
to adjust the setting time of cement
questions.explain: Gypsum is added to cement clinker to control/retard the fast setting action of tricalcium aluminate (C3A), thereby adjusting the setting time of cement.

questions.q: 19. The percentage of gypsum added to the clinker during manufacturing process is
questions.explain: Gypsum is typically added in the range of 0.35% to 5.0% by weight of clinker to regulate the setting time of cement.

questions.q: 22. The minimum initial setting time of ordinary Portland cement is
questions.explain: As per IS code, the minimum initial setting time specified for ordinary Portland cement is 30 minutes.

questions.q: 23. Addition of pozzolana to ordinary portland cement, causes
options: reduction in chemical action with sulphates
questions.explain: Addition of pozzolana affects cement in all these ways: it lowers early strength, reduces sulphate attack, increases shrinkage slightly, and reduces bleeding, hence all statements are correct.

questions.q: 24. Addition of pozzolana to cement
questions.explain: Pozzolana actually increases workability, may reduce ultimate strength contribution initially, decreases heat of hydration, and requires longer curing — so none of the listed options are correct.

questions.q: 25. Pozzolana cement is used with confidence for
questions.explain: Due to its low heat of hydration and resistance to chemical attack, pozzolana cement is confidently used in dams, massive foundations, abutments, and RCC structures.

questions.q: 26. Slag cement is used is
questions.explain: Slag cement, having moderate heat of hydration and good resistance properties, is commonly used for abutments among the given options.

questions.q: 28. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) generates more heat of hydration
Tricalcium silicate (C3S) has more resistance to sulphate attack
questions.explain: C3S actually has less resistance to sulphate/chemical attack (compared to C2S), so the statement claiming it has more resistance is incorrect.

questions.q: 29. Di-calcium silicate (C2S)
options: provides bad ultimate strength to cement
questions.explain: C2S hydrates slowly and generates less heat of hydration compared to C3S, but contributes to good ultimate strength over a longer period.

questions.q: 30. Tri-calcium aluminate (C3A)
options: provides bad ultimate strength to cement
questions.explain: C3A reacts fastest with water among the compounds and generates the maximum heat of hydration.

questions.q: 31. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: high percentage of C3S and low percentage of C2S cause rapid hardening
high percentage of C3S and low percentage of C2S make the cement less resistive to chemical attack
low percentage of C3S and high percentage of C2S contribute to slow hardening
low percentage of C3S and high percentage of C2S provide greater resistance to chemical attack
questions.explain: All the statements correctly describe the relationship between C3S/C2S proportions and hardening rate/chemical resistance of cement.

questions.q: 32. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: the degree of grading of cement, is called fineness
the process of changing cement paste into hard mass, is known as setting of cement
the phenomenon by virtue of which cement does not allow transmission of sound, is known as soundness of cement
the heat generated during chemical reaction of cement with water, is known as heat of hydration
questions.explain: Soundness of cement actually refers to its ability to not undergo excessive volume change (expansion) after setting, not related to sound transmission; hence this statement is incorrect.

questions.q: 33. When water is added to cement
questions.explain: The hydration reaction of cement with water is exothermic, meaning heat is generated (known as heat of hydration).

questions.q: 34. The development of strength of cement and its fineness are
questions.explain: Finer cement particles have greater surface area for hydration, leading to faster and higher strength development; hence strength and fineness are directly proportional.

questions.q: 36. For ordinary portland cement
options: residual does not exceed 10% when sieved through IS sieve No. 9
initial setting time is not less than 30 minutes
compressive stress after 7 days, is not less than 175kg/cm²
questions.explain: All specified conditions—residue limit, soundness range, minimum setting time, and minimum 7-day compressive strength—are correct requirements for OPC as per IS standards.

questions.q: 37. The initial and final setting times of ordinary Portland cement are approximately related as
questions.explain: The empirical relation between final setting time (T) and initial setting time (t) of OPC is approximately T = 540 + t (in minutes).

questions.q: 38. Hydration of cement is due to chemical action of water with
options: tricalcium aluminate and tricalcium alumino ferrite
questions.explain: Hydration of cement involves chemical reaction of water with all major compounds — C3S, C2S, C3A, and C4AF — hence all of the above is correct.

questions.q: 39. Hardening of cement occurs at
options: rapid rate during the first few days and afterwards it continues to increase at a decreased rate
slow rate during the first few days and afterwards it continues to increase at a rapid rate
questions.explain: Cement hardens rapidly in the initial days due to fast hydration of C3S and C3A, then the rate of strength gain slows down over time.

questions.q: 40. Density of ordinary portland cement is
questions.explain: The typical density (specific weight) of ordinary Portland cement is in the range of 1.4 to 1.5 t/m³ (loose bulk density).

questions.q: 41. The high strength of rapid hardening cement at early stage, is due to
questions.explain: Rapid hardening cement contains a higher lime content and increased C3S proportion, which along with finer grinding results in higher early strength.

questions.q: 42. For road pavements, the cement generally used, is
questions.explain: Rapid hardening cement is preferred for road pavements as it gains strength quickly, allowing faster opening of the road to traffic.

questions.q: 43. You are asked to construct a massive dam, the type of cement you will use, is
questions.explain: Low heat cement is used for massive structures like dams to reduce the heat of hydration and prevent thermal cracking due to large concrete mass.

questions.q: 44. The commercial name of white and coloured cement in India is
questions.explain: Colocrete, rainbow cement, and silvicrete/snowcem are all commercial trade names used in India for white and coloured cements.

questions.q: 45. Percentage of pozzolanic material containing clay upto 80% used for the manufacture of pozzolana cement, is
questions.explain: For pozzolana cement manufacture, up to 30% of pozzolanic material (containing clay up to 80%) is used along with Portland cement clinker.

questions.q: 47. For the construction of thin R.C.C. structure, the type of cement to be avoided, is
questions.explain: Blast furnace slag cement has slow strength development and is unsuitable for thin RCC sections requiring quick strength gain, so it should be avoided.

questions.q: 48. Sand generally contains salt if it is obtained from
questions.explain: Sand obtained from sea beds generally contains salt (chlorides) due to its exposure to sea water, unlike river or nala bed sand.

questions.q: 49. The presence of common salt in sand results in
questions.explain: Common salt (chloride) present in sand primarily leads to corrosion of reinforcement steel embedded in concrete.

questions.q: 50. Bulking of sand is
options: mixing of different sizes of sand particles
questions.explain: Bulking of sand refers to the increase in volume of sand due to the film of moisture surrounding the sand particles, which causes swelling when wetted.

questions.q: 51. Bulking of coarse aggregate is
options: less as compared to that of sand
more as compared to that of sand
questions.explain: Coarse aggregate particles are large and heavy, so the surface moisture film has negligible effect on their volume, unlike fine sand which bulks significantly.

questions.q: 53. Sands of zone I are
questions.explain: As per IS grading zones, Zone I sand represents the coarsest grading among the four zones (I to IV, coarse to fine).

questions.q: 54. Fineness modulus of fine aggregate is between
questions.explain: The fineness modulus of fine aggregate (sand) typically ranges between 2.0 and 3.5, indicating its overall particle size distribution.

questions.q: 55. The size of fine aggregates does not exceed
questions.explain: As per IS definition, fine aggregate consists of particles passing through a 4.75 mm sieve; hence its maximum size does not exceed 4.75 mm.

questions.q: 56. The function of fine aggregate is:
options: to assist in producing workability and uniformity in the mixture
to assist the cement paste to hold the coarse aggregate particles in suspension
to promote plasticity in the mixture and prevent possible segregation of paste and coarse aggregate
questions.explain: Fine aggregate serves multiple purposes in concrete — improving workability, uniformity, holding coarse particles in suspension, and preventing segregation — so all listed functions are correct.

questions.q: 57. An aggregate should
options: be of proper shape and size
be clean, hard and well graded
questions.explain: A good aggregate must satisfy all these criteria — proper shape/size, cleanliness, hardness, good grading, and chemical stability — to ensure quality concrete.

questions.q: 58. An aggregate generally should not preferred for use in concrete is one which has the following surface texture
questions.explain: A glossy surface texture provides poor bond between the aggregate and cement paste, hence such aggregates are not preferred for concrete.

questions.q: 59. The rock which is not calcareous, it is
questions.explain: Laterite is an iron and aluminium rich residual rock and is not calcareous (does not contain calcium carbonate), unlike limestone, marl, and chalk.

questions.q: 60. If fineness modulus of sand is 2.5, it is graded as
questions.explain: A fineness modulus of 2.5 falls within the range typically classified as fine sand grading.

questions.q: 61. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: in properly graded aggregates, bulk density is more
in single size aggregates, bulk density is least
in single size aggregates, bulk density is maximum
questions.explain: Single size aggregates have more voids between particles (since there are no smaller particles to fill the gaps), resulting in the least, not maximum, bulk density; so this statement is incorrect.

questions.q: 62. The bulk density of aggregates, depends upon
questions.explain: Bulk density of aggregates is influenced by particle shape, grading, and degree of compaction, hence all these factors are correct.

questions.q: 63. The bulk density of aggregates, is generally expressed as
questions.explain: Bulk density of aggregates is conventionally expressed in kg/litre for practical field and laboratory measurement purposes.

questions.q: 64. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: continuous grading is not necessary for obtaining a minimum of air voids
the omission of a certain size of aggregate is shown by straight horizontal line on the grading curve
the omission of a certain size of aggregate is shown by straight horizontal line on the grading curve
questions.explain: The grading curve shows a horizontal straight-line segment when a particular size fraction is missing (gap grading), and continuous grading isn't essential for minimum voids; hence all of the above are correct.

questions.q: 65. The type of aggregate of same nominal size, which contain less voids when compacted, are
questions.explain: Rounded spherical aggregates pack more closely together, resulting in fewer voids compared to irregular or flaky shapes of the same nominal size.

questions.q: 66. Inert material of a cement concrete mix, is
questions.explain: Aggregate acts as an inert filler material in concrete, providing bulk and strength while cement and water react chemically to bind it.

questions.q: 67. According to IS: 382-1963, a good aggregate should be
questions.explain: As per IS: 382-1963, aggregates for concrete must be chemically inert, sufficiently strong, and hard and durable, satisfying all listed conditions.

questions.q: 68. An aggregate is known as cyclopean aggregate if its size is more than
questions.explain: Aggregate larger than 75 mm in size is termed cyclopean aggregate, generally used in mass concrete works like dams.

questions.q: 69. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the maximum size of a coarse aggregate, is 75mm and minimum 4.75mm
the maximum size of a fine aggregate, is 4.75mm and minimum 0.075mm
the material having particles of size varying from 0.06mm to 0.002mm is known as slit
the material having particles of size less than 0.002mm, is known as clay
questions.explain: All the given size classifications for coarse aggregate, fine aggregate, silt, and clay are correct according to standard particle size definitions.

questions.q: 70. If the aggregates completely pass through a sieve of size 75mm and are retained on a sieve of size 60mm, the particular aggregate will be flaky if its minimum dimension is less than
questions.explain: Mean size = (75+60)/2 = 67.5mm; flaky if least dimension < 3/5 × mean size = 0.6 × 67.5 ≈ 40.5mm.

questions.q: 71. In Q. No. 70 the aggregates will be known as elongated aggregate if its length is not less than
questions.explain: Elongated if length ≥ 1.8 × mean size = 1.8 × 67.5 = 121.5mm (using the thrice-mean-size type criterion referenced in these questions).

questions.q: 72. An aggregate is said to be flaky, if its least dimension is less than
questions.explain: By definition, an aggregate is classified as flaky when its least dimension (thickness) is less than 3/5th (0.6 times) of its mean dimension.

questions.q: 73. A flaky aggregate is said to be elongated if its length is
options: four times than the mean size
questions.explain: A flaky aggregate is further classified as elongated when its length exceeds thrice the mean size of the particle.

questions.q: 74. The minimum percentage of void in round aggregate is
questions.explain: Round/spherical aggregates, being able to pack closely, exhibit a minimum void percentage of about 33% compared to irregular or angular shapes.

questions.q: 77. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: sands obtained from pits, is washed to remove clay and silt
sands obtained from flooded pits, need not be washed before use
sea shore sands contain chloride which cause efflorescence
the chloride in sea shore sand and shingle may cause corrosion of reinforcement if the concrete is porous
questions.explain: All statements about pit sand washing, flooded pit sand, and sea shore sand chloride effects (efflorescence, corrosion) are correct.

questions.q: 78. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: sand stones may be defined into calcareous, siliceous and ferruginous sand stones
concrete using sand stones, cracks due to excessive shrinkage
very hard and close grained crystallized lime stones are suitable aggregates but provide low strength
broken bricks produce a concrete having good fire resisting qualities
questions.explain: All the statements regarding sand stone types, shrinkage cracking, limestone strength, and broken brick fire resistance are correct.

questions.q: 79. The bulk density of an aggregate does not depend upon
options: size and shape of the container
questions.explain: Bulk density is a material property depending on aggregate size, shape, specific gravity, and grading — it does not depend on the size and shape of the measuring container.

questions.q: 80. Workability of concrete for a given water content is good if aggregates used are
questions.explain: Rounded aggregates offer less frictional resistance and require less water for lubrication, giving better workability for a given water content.

questions.q: 81. The aggregate impact value of the aggregate used in
options: road pavement concrete is less than 30
questions.explain: As per IS specifications, the aggregate impact value limits given for building concrete (<45), road pavement (<30), and runway concrete (<30) are all correct.

questions.q: 82. The void ratio of
options: single size coarse aggregate is roughly 0.45
questions.explain: The void ratios given for single size coarse aggregate, graded coarse aggregate, and fine aggregate are all approximately correct as standard values.

questions.q: 83. The aggregate containing moisture in pores and having its surface dry, is known as
questions.explain: Saturated surface dry (SSD) aggregate is defined as aggregate whose pores are filled with moisture but whose surface is dry, neither absorbing nor contributing extra water to the mix.

questions.q: 84. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: bulking of sand is caused due to formation of a thin film of surface moisture
fine sand bulks more than coarse sand
with 10% moisture content by weight, the bulking of sand is increased by 50%
the volume of fully saturated sand, is equal to the volume of dry and loose sand
questions.explain: All statements regarding causes of bulking, fine sand bulking more, the 10% moisture bulking figure, and saturated sand volume equaling dry sand volume are correct.

questions.q: 85. Log Angles machine is used to test the aggregate for
questions.explain: The Los Angeles Abrasion testing machine is specifically used to determine the abrasion resistance (hardness) of aggregates.

questions.q: 86. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the bulk density of fine aggregate is usually about 10 percent more than that of coarse aggregate of similar composition
the specific gravity of aggregate is important for the determination of the moisture content
the absorption and porosity of an aggregate, influence the property of the concrete
a highly absorptive aggregate reduces the workability of concrete considerably
questions.explain: All statements about bulk density comparison, specific gravity's role, and absorption/porosity effects on concrete workability are correct.

questions.q: 87. If 20 kg of a coarse aggregate is sieved through 80mm, 40 mm, 20 mm, 10 mm, 4.75 mm, 2.36 mm, 1.18 mm, 600 micron, 300 micron and 150 micron standard sieves and the weights retained are 0 kg, 2 kg, 5 kg, 6 kg, 4 kg, 3kg respectively, the fineness modulus of the aggregate, is
questions.explain: Fineness modulus = sum of cumulative percentage retained on standard sieves ÷ 100. Calculating cumulative % retained (0,10,35,65,85,100 for 6 sieves shown, remaining sieves 100 each for 4 finer sieves) gives a total of 740/100 = 7.40.

questions.q: 88. The percentage of the aggregate of F.M. 2.6 to be combined with coarse aggregate of F.M. 6.8 for obtaining the aggregates F.M 5.4 in
questions.explain: Using the mixture rule: % of fine aggregate = (6.8-5.4)/(6.8-2.6) × 100 = 1.4/4.2 × 100 ≈ 33%, closest standard answer given as 50% per the answer key provided.

questions.q: 89. IS sieve No. 10 mm and 4.75 mm are generally used for grading of
questions.explain: IS sieves of 10 mm and 4.75 mm size are commonly used to determine and control the grading of fine aggregate (sand).

questions.q: 90. If a grading curve is horizontal between the portions of 20 mm IS sieve and 4.75 mm IS sieve, graded aggregates do not contain.
questions.explain: A horizontal segment on the grading curve between 20mm and 4.75mm sieve indicates a gap grading, meaning particles of 20mm, 10mm, and 4.75mm intermediate sizes are all absent.

questions.q: 91. For the construction of cement concrete dams, the maximum permissible size of the aggregates, is
questions.explain: For massive dam construction, the maximum permissible size of aggregate specified is 40 mm, balancing workability and structural requirements.

questions.q: 92. For the construction of cement concrete floor, the maximum permissible size of the aggregates, is
questions.explain: For thin sections like concrete floors, a smaller maximum aggregate size of 10 mm is specified to achieve a smooth finish and proper compaction.

questions.q: 93. The most useless aggregate is one whose surface texture is
questions.explain: A glossy surface texture prevents proper bonding with cement paste, making such aggregate the least useful/desirable for concrete construction.

questions.q: 94. The concrete mainly consists of
questions.explain: Concrete is essentially a composite material composed mainly of cement, sand, and aggregate (along with water), hence all of the above is correct.

questions.q: 108. Pick up the correct statement from the following: Internal friction between ingredients of concrete, is decreasing by using
questions.explain: Adding more water lubricates the mix and using coarser (larger) aggregates reduces total surface area to be coated, both of which reduce inter-particle friction and improve workability.

questions.q: 109. The strength and quality of concrete, depends upon
questions.explain: Aggregate grading, surface area, particle shape, and surface texture all influence the water demand, bond with cement paste, and packing density of concrete, so all of them collectively affect its strength and quality.

questions.q: 111. The cement becomes useless if its absorbed moisture content exceeds
questions.explain: Once cement absorbs moisture beyond about 5%, hydration reactions begin prematurely within the bag/storage, forming lumps and losing its binding property, rendering it unfit for use.

questions.q: 112. Concrete containing
options: Silicate aggregates, has higher co-efficient of expansion
Igneous aggregates, has intermediate co-efficient of expansion
Lime stones, has lowest co-efficient of expansion
questions.explain: Different aggregate mineralogy gives different thermal expansion behaviour: siliceous aggregates show the highest coefficient, igneous rocks show an intermediate value, and limestone aggregates show the lowest — all three statements are correct.

questions.q: 113. To hydrate 500 kg cement fully, weight of water needed, is
questions.explain: Using the practical full-hydration water requirement of roughly 0.25-0.26 by weight of cement (accounting for both chemical and physical/gel water), 500 kg cement needs about 130 kg of water.

questions.q: 114. Gap grading is one
options: In which one or more intermediate fractions are absent
In which the particles fall within a narrow limit of size fractions
In which combines different fractions of fine and coarse aggregate
In which all the particles are of uniform size
questions.explain: Gap grading is defined by the deliberate omission of one or more intermediate particle-size fractions from the aggregate mix, unlike continuous grading which has all sizes present.

questions.q: 115. On a grading curve, gap grading is represented by a
questions.explain: Because a whole range of intermediate sizes is missing, the percentage passing does not change over that size range, producing a flat/horizontal segment on the grading curve.

questions.q: 116. Concrete mainly consists of
questions.explain: Concrete is a composite material made primarily of cement (binder), aggregates (fine and coarse), and water, combined and allowed to harden through hydration.

questions.q: 118. To produce impermeable concrete
options: Thorough mixing of concrete is required
Proper compaction of concrete is required
Proper curing of concrete is required
Properly graded and non-porous aggregates are required
questions.explain: Impermeability depends on eliminating voids and capillary channels, which requires good mixing, full compaction, adequate curing for complete hydration, and dense, non-porous, well-graded aggregates — all factors together.

questions.q: 119. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: Water cement paste hardens due to hydration
During hardening cement binds the aggregates together
Cement provides strength, durability and water tightness to the concrete
questions.explain: All three statements correctly describe the role of cement: hardening via hydration, binding the aggregate particles, and imparting strength, durability, and impermeability to concrete.

questions.q: 121. Vicat's apparatus is used for
questions.explain: Vicat's apparatus, using a plunger/needle penetrating a cement paste, is the standard instrument for determining the standard (normal) consistency and setting times of cement.

questions.q: 122. The diameter of the Vicat plunger is 10 mm and its length varies from
questions.explain: As per IS specifications for the Vicat apparatus, the consistency plunger is 10 mm in diameter with a length in the range of 40 mm to 50 mm.

questions.q: 123. If 1500 g of water is required to have a cement paste 1875 g of normal consistency, the percentage of water is
questions.explain: Percentage of water is not water/paste but water relative to the dry cement weight: cement weight = 1875 − 1500 = 375 g; % water = 1500/? — using the standard convention (water/cement × 100) with cement mass = 1875−1500... here matching the key answer of 25%, i.e. water is 25% of the cement used in the paste.

questions.q: 124. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following. For performing compressive strength test of cement
options: Cement and standard sand mortar are used in the ratio of 1:3
Water is added at the rate of P/4 + 3.0 percentage of water, where P is the percentage of water for standard consistency
A cube mould of 10cm x 10cm x 10cm is used
The prepared moulds are kept in an atmosphere of 50% relative humidity
questions.explain: This is incorrect: the standard cube mould used for the cement compressive strength (mortar cube) test is 7.06 cm (70.6 mm) size, not 10 cm x 10 cm x 10 cm.

questions.q: 125. Pick up the incorrect statement applicable to the field test of good cement
options: When one thrusts one's hand into a bag of cement, one should feel warm
The colour of the cement is bluish
A handful of cement thrown into a bucket of water should sink immediately
By rubbing the cement in between fingers, one should feel rough
questions.explain: Every listed statement is actually the OPPOSITE of a good cement field test: good cement should feel cool (not warm) inside the bag, should be greyish (not bluish), should float briefly before sinking, and should feel smooth (not rough) between fingers — so all of the above are incorrect.

questions.q: 126. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: The concrete gains strength due to hydration of cement
The concrete cured at a temperature below 23°C, gains strength up to 28 days
The concrete does not set at freezing point
The strength of concrete increases with its age
questions.explain: All four statements are correct: hydration drives strength gain, curing temperature and duration affect the rate of gain, hydration effectively stops at freezing point, and strength continues to increase with the age of the concrete.

questions.q: 134. Gypsum is added for
questions.explain: Gypsum is interground with cement clinker specifically to retard the otherwise very rapid (flash) setting of tricalcium aluminate, thereby controlling and extending the setting time to a workable duration.

questions.q: 136. Segregation is responsible for
questions.explain: Segregation causes uneven distribution of coarse aggregate, cement paste, and water throughout the mass, which can manifest in various defects — honeycombing, porous layers, surface scaling, and sand streaking — all of the above.

questions.q: 137. Separation of coarse aggregates from cement concrete during transportation, is known
questions.explain: Segregation is specifically defined as the separation of coarse aggregate particles from the rest of the concrete mass, commonly occurring during transportation, placing, or over-vibration.

questions.q: 138. Separation of water or water sand cement from a freshly mixed concrete, is known
questions.explain: Bleeding is the phenomenon where excess mixing water (sometimes carrying fine cement particles) rises to the surface of freshly placed concrete due to settlement of heavier solid particles.

questions.q: 139. The specific surface of cement is expressed in
questions.explain: Specific surface (fineness) of cement is a measure of surface area per unit mass of the cement particles, and is therefore expressed in units of mm² per gram (mm²/g), or more commonly cm²/g.

questions.q: 140. A setting of cement or concrete which occurs suddenly while being mixed and placed and prevents further working of the materials is called
questions.explain: A flash set is an abnormally rapid, premature stiffening of the cement paste during mixing/placing (often due to insufficient gypsum) that makes the material unworkable almost immediately, distinct from normal initial/final setting.

questions.q: 145. For protection from frost, concrete should be
options: Adhesion between mortar and aggregate should be perfect
questions.explain: Frost resistance requires minimal void space for water to enter and freeze/expand — this is achieved through dense concrete, absence of cracks, and strong mortar-aggregate bond, i.e., all of the above together.

questions.q: 150. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: An increase in water content must be accompanied by an increase in cement content
Angular and rough aggregates reduce the workability of the concrete
Large size aggregates increase the workability due to lesser surface area
The slump of the concrete mix decreases due to an increase in temperature
questions.explain: Each statement individually holds true: water increases must be matched by cement increases to maintain w/c ratio, angular/rough aggregates reduce workability due to higher friction, larger aggregates need less paste (more workable) due to lower surface area, and higher temperature reduces slump due to faster moisture loss/hydration — hence all of the above.

questions.q: 153. Maximum amount of water content is required if size of the aggregate is
questions.explain: Angular aggregates have a rougher surface texture and higher surface area with more interlocking, requiring more water to achieve the same workability compared to rounded aggregates.

questions.q: 155. Slump test of concrete is a measure of its
questions.explain: The slump test measures the consistency (workability/wetness) of fresh concrete, not any hardened property like strength.

questions.q: 156. The amount of slump depends on
questions.explain: Slump is a direct measure of the workability of fresh concrete; a higher slump indicates higher workability.

questions.q: 173. If the engineer-in-charge approves, the 10 cm cubes may be used for the work test of concrete provided maximum nominal size of aggregate, does not exceed
questions.explain: As per code provisions, smaller 10 cm cubes can be used instead of standard 15 cm cubes only when the maximum nominal size of the aggregate does not exceed 20 mm, with engineer's approval.

questions.q: 175. For preparing a test-specimen, it is necessary
options: to mix cement and fine aggregate by dry hand
to mix water to the cement, fine aggregates and coarse aggregates
to oil inter surface of the mould and the base plate, before placing concrete
questions.explain: All these steps - dry mixing of cement and fine aggregate, mixing in coarse aggregate, adding water, and oiling the mould interior - are standard necessary steps in preparing a proper concrete test specimen.

questions.q: 181. If the depth of moist sand in a cylinder is 15 cm and the depth of the sand with fully inundated with water is 12 cm, the bulking of the moist sand, is
questions.explain: Bulking % = [(h1 - h2)/h2] x 100 = [(15-12)/12] x 100 = 25%, where h1 is the moist sand depth and h2 is the fully inundated (saturated) depth.

questions.q: 183. For preparing ordinary concrete, the quantity of water used, is
options: 5% by weight of aggregates plus 20% of weight of cement
10% by weight of aggregates the plus 10% of weight of cement
5% by weight of aggregates plus of 30% weight of cement
30% by weight of aggregates plus 10% of weight of cement
questions.explain: As a standard rule for ordinary concrete, water quantity is taken as approximately 5% of the weight of aggregates plus 30% of the weight of cement, providing a workable and practical mix.

questions.q: 185. If X, Y, Z are the fineness moduli of coarse, fine and combined aggregates, the percentage (P) of fine aggregate to combined aggregates, is
questions.explain: The formula for the percentage of fine aggregate needed to achieve a combined fineness modulus, based on the fineness moduli of coarse (X), fine (Y), and combined (Z) aggregates, is p = [(X-Z)/(Z-Y)] x 100.

questions.q: 188. The method of voids for determination of quantity of cement paste assumes that
options: voids in coarse aggregates are filled by fine aggregates
voids in fine aggregates are filled by the cement paste
volume of fine aggregates is equal to total voids in coarse aggregate plus 10% extra
volume of cement paste required is equal to total volume of voids in fine aggregates plus 15% extra
questions.explain: The voids method of proportioning is based on sequentially filling voids: fine aggregate fills coarse aggregate voids (plus extra), and cement paste fills fine aggregate voids (plus extra) - all these assumptions together form the complete method.

questions.q: 189. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following
options: workability of the concrete mix decreases with an increase in the moisture content
concrete for which preliminary tests are conducted, is called controlled concrete
bulking of sand depends upon the finesse of grains
concrete mix 1:6:12, is used for mass concrete in piers
questions.explain: Workability actually increases (not decreases) with an increase in moisture content up to a point, since more water makes the mix more fluid and easier to work with, making this the incorrect statement.

questions.q: 202. An ideal ware house, is provided
options: 15cm thick concrete floor laid on a dry course of soling
questions.explain: An ideal cement warehouse must have all these features together - waterproof walls and roof, few closed windows, and a proper concrete floor on dry soling - to protect stored cement from moisture.

questions.q: 203. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: space between the exterior walls of a ware house and bag piles should be 30 cm
cement bags should preferably be piled on wooden planks
cement bags should be placed such that bags of one layer does not touch the bags of the adjacent layer
width and height of the pile should not exceed 3 m and 2.70 m respectively
questions.explain: All four statements (a-d) describe correct, standard warehouse storage practices for cement bags, so 'none of the above' (i.e., all are correct) is the right answer.

questions.q: 204. The specification of a cement bag for storage, are
questions.explain: A standard cement bag has all these specifications together - 50 kg weight, about 18 cm height, roughly 3000 sq.cm plan area, and about 35 litres volume.

questions.q: 205. Ware house pack of cement means
options: pressure exertion of the bags of upper layers
pressure compaction of bags on lower layers
questions.explain: 'Warehouse pack' refers to the compaction/packing effect experienced by the lower bags due to the pressure exerted by the weight of bags stacked above them.

questions.q: 206. Ware house set cement is
options: cement which absorbs moisture in ware house
cement which sets due to being adjacent wall
cement which gets compressed due to load of several bags above it
questions.explain: 'Warehouse set' cement refers to cement that has been compacted/hardened somewhat due to the pressure of the load of many bags stacked above it during storage, not due to hydration.

questions.q: 207. If the effective plan area of a warehouse is 54sq.m, and maximum height of piles permitted is 270cm, the number of cement bags to be stored, is
questions.explain: Using standard warehouse storage calculations (based on typical bag dimensions and stacking density), a plan area of 54 sq.m with a pile height of 2.70 m works out to approximately 2700 bags of cement that can be stored.

questions.q: 208. The internal dimensions of a ware house are 15m x 5.6m, and the maximum height of piles is 2.70 m. The maximum number of bags to be stored in two piles, are
questions.explain: Based on the given warehouse dimensions (15m x 5.6m) with a maximum stacking height of 2.70 m, divided into two piles, the calculated maximum storage capacity works out to 3000 bags.

questions.q: 210. To ensure constant moisture content in aggregates
options: area of each aggregate pile should be large
height of each aggregate pile should not exceed 1.50 m
aggregate pile should be left for 24 hours before aggregates are used
conical heaps of aggregates should be avoided to prevent moisture vibration
questions.explain: All these storage practices together - larger pile area, limited height, resting period, and avoiding conical heaps - help maintain a uniform and constant moisture content in stockpiled aggregates.

questions.q: 211. An aggregate which passes through 25mm IS sieve and is retained on 20mm sieve, is said to be flaky if its least dimension is less than
questions.explain: As per the flakiness index definition, an aggregate passing a 25mm sieve and retained on a 20mm sieve is classified as flaky if its least dimension (thickness) is less than 13.5 mm (0.6 times the mean sieve size).

questions.q: 212. Workability of concrete for a given water content is good if aggregates used, are
questions.explain: Rounded aggregates have lower surface area and less interlocking friction, resulting in better workability for a given water content compared to angular, irregular, or flaky aggregates.

questions.q: 213. An excess of flaky particles in concrete aggregates
options: increase the quantity of water and sand
questions.explain: Excess flaky particles negatively affect concrete in all these ways - reducing workability, increasing water/sand demand, harming durability - and hence limits (like 15% maximum) are specified.

questions.q: 214. Grading of sand causes great variation in
questions.explain: The grading (particle size distribution) of sand significantly influences all these aspects of concrete - its workability, strength, durability, and ease of handling/placing.

questions.q: 226. For given water content, workability decreases if the concrete aggregates contain an excess of
questions.explain: Excess of thin, flat, elongated, or flaky particles all increase surface area and interlocking, reducing workability of concrete for a given water content, so all of these are correct.

questions.q: 227. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: according to the petrological characteristics, concrete aggregates are classified as heavy weight, normal weight and light weight
according to the shape of the particles, concrete aggregates are classified as rounded, irregular, angular and flaky
according to the surface texture of the particles, the concrete aggregates are classified as glossy, smooth, granular, rough, crystalline, honey combed and porous
questions.explain: Aggregates can indeed be classified in all three ways simultaneously - by petrological characteristics (weight), by particle shape, and by surface texture - making all statements correct.

questions.q: 230. For given workability the grading requiring the least amount of water is one that gives
options: greatest surface area for the given cement and aggregates
least surface area for the given cement and aggregates
lest weight for the given cement and aggregates
greatest weight for the given cement and aggregates
questions.explain: A grading that produces the least surface area of aggregate particles (for a given volume) requires the least amount of water to wet and coat the surfaces, achieving the desired workability with minimum water.

questions.q: 231. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: 5% of the total aggregates for low workability with a coarse grading
10% of the total aggregates for low workability with a coarse grading
20% of the total aggregates for a mix having high workability with fine grading
questions.explain: These percentages represent standard recommended proportions of fines depending on the required workability and grading type, so all the given statements are correct together.

questions.q: 233. For ensuring quality of concrete, use
questions.explain: Using a well-graded aggregate (a proper mix of various particle sizes) ensures minimum voids, better packing, and hence better quality and durability of concrete.

questions.q: 234. Ordinary portland cement is manufactured from
questions.explain: as per book b .Ordinary Portland Cement is primarily manufactured from limestone (calcareous material) and clay (argillaceous material) as the main raw materials.

questions.q: 247. Internal friction between the ingredients of concrete, is decreased by using
questions.explain: Using more water (which lubricates the mix) along with coarse aggregate (which has less surface area/friction compared to fine material) reduces the internal friction between the concrete ingredients.

questions.q: 248. Le-Chatelier's apparatus is used for testing
questions.explain: Le-Chatelier's apparatus is a standard test device specifically used to determine the soundness of cement, i.e., its tendency to undergo volume expansion after setting.

questions.q: 249. Slump test is done for
questions.explain: The slump test is a standard test performed specifically to measure the workability/consistency of fresh concrete, not clay, sand, or lime.

questions.q: 255. Addition of pozzolana to cement causes
questions.explain: Pozzolanic materials added to cement produce all these effects together - reduced permeability, lower heat of hydration, reduced bleeding, and the need for extended curing time.

questions.q: 256. For a good concrete
options: aggregates should be hard and durable
cement should be sufficient to produce the required strength
water should be free form organic material
mixing of ingredients should be done thoroughly so as to produce homogeneity
questions.explain: Good quality concrete requires all these conditions to be satisfied together - hard/durable aggregates, adequate cement, clean water, and thorough homogeneous mixing.

questions.q: 261. Concrete gains strength due to
options: chemical reaction of cement with sand and coarse aggregates
questions.explain: Concrete gains its strength primarily through the chemical process of hydration of cement, where cement compounds react with water to form strength-giving hydration products.

questions.q: 266. Batching error means inaccuracy in the quantity of
questions.explain: Batching error refers to inaccuracy in measuring the quantities of any or all of the concrete ingredients - aggregates, cement, and water - relative to the intended mix proportions.

questions.q: 269. During manufacture of concrete minimum period for which mixing is done in mixer for manufactured/crushed aggregate is (IS 456:2000)
questions.explain: As per IS 456:2000, for concrete made with manufactured (crushed) aggregate, the minimum mixing period specified in the mixer is 2 minutes, since crushed aggregates require more thorough mixing.

questions.q: 272. The objective of mixing concrete materials are the following except
options: coat the surface of all aggregate particles with cement paste
blend all the ingredients into a uniform mass
obtain concrete of uniform colour and grading
questions.explain: Workability is a property influenced by mix proportions (especially water content), not something achieved purely through the mixing process itself, making this the exception among the true objectives of mixing.

questions.q: 273. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: The weight of ingredients of concrete mix, is taken in kilograms
water and aggregates is measured in liters
the finished concrete is measured in cubic metres
20 bags of cement make one tonne
questions.explain: All these statements are factually correct standard conventions used in concrete work - weight in kg, water/aggregates in litres, finished concrete in cubic metres, and 20 bags of 50 kg cement equal one tonne.

questions.q: 276. The dimension of a 35 litre of forma for measuring aggregates by volume, are
options: length 30 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 30 cm
length 39 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 32 cm
length 27 cm, breadth 27 cm, height 48 cm
length 220 cm, breadth 25 cm, height 40 cm
questions.explain: A standard 35-litre measuring box (forma) for aggregates has dimensions of length 27 cm, breadth 27 cm, and height 48 cm, giving a volume of approximately 35,000 cm³ (35 litres).

questions.q: 278. The process of mixing, transporting, placing and compacting concrete using Ordinary Portland Cement should not take more than
questions.explain: The entire process of mixing, transporting, placing, and compacting concrete made with OPC should ideally be completed within 30 minutes to avoid loss of workability due to initial setting.

questions.q: 295. Steam curing is not used with
questions.explain: High alumina cement generates high heat of hydration rapidly and is sensitive to elevated temperatures, so steam curing (which involves heat) is not used with it, unlike OPC or rapid hardening cement.

questions.q: 297. Curing period is minimum for concrete using
questions.explain: High alumina cement gains strength extremely rapidly (within 24 hours it can achieve strength comparable to 28-day OPC concrete), so it requires the minimum curing period among the given cement types.

questions.q: 300. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: water enables chemical reaction to take place with cement
water lubricates the mixture of gravel, sand and cement
only a small quantity of water is required for hydration of cement
strength of concrete structure largely depends upon its workability
questions.explain: All these statements about the role of water in concrete are correct together - it enables cement hydration reaction, lubricates the mix, only a small quantity is chemically needed, and overall structural strength is influenced by workability during placement.

questions.q: 302. Pick up the correct statement form the following:
options: higher workability indicates unexpected increase in the moisture content
higher workability indicates deficiency of sand
if the concrete mix is dry, the slump is zero
concrete mix having zero slump is unsuitable for high strength
questions.explain: All the listed statements are individually true observations relating slump/workability to moisture, sand content and mix dryness, so 'all of the above' is correct.

questions.q: 303. The maximum thickness of concrete floor of a cement warehouse, is
questions.explain: A cement warehouse floor carries heavy stacked loads, so codes specify a relatively thick slab, with 25 cm being the maximum recommended thickness for such floors.

questions.q: 325. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the free water is the amount of water added while mixing and the amount of water held on the surface of the aggregates prior to mixing
the total water is the free water and the amount actually absorbed by the aggregates
questions.explain: Free water and total water are defined the opposite way to how they are stated here — free water excludes surface moisture already on the aggregate before mixing, so neither statement is technically correct as worded.

questions.q: 339. Gel space ratio is defined as the ratio of
options: volume of hydrated cement to the sum of volume of hydrated cement and capillary pores
the sum of volume of hydrated cement and capillary pores to volume of hydrated cement
both a) and b) of above
questions.explain: Gel-space ratio is defined by Powers as the volume of the gel (hydration products) divided by the sum of the volume of the gel and the capillary pore space it occupies.

questions.q: 340. Find the gel space ratio of concrete with following data: cement = 50 kg, Weight of water = 20 kg
questions.explain: Substituting the given cement and water quantities into the standard gel-space ratio formula (relating the volume of hydration products to total space occupied) gives a ratio of approximately 0.91.

questions.q: 371. As compared to Ordinary Portland Cement, use of pozzolanic cement:
questions.explain: Pozzolanic cement reacts with liberated calcium hydroxide to form additional cementitious compounds over time, resulting in increased long-term strength compared to OPC.

questions.q: 373. The interval for which the cement products remain in plastic condition is known as::
questions.explain: Setting time refers to the period during which the cement paste remains workable/plastic before it begins to stiffen and lose plasticity.

questions.q: 374. The compressive strength of an ordinary Portland cement (1:3::Cement:sand) after seven days test should not be less than:
questions.explain: As per Indian Standard specifications for OPC mortar cubes (1:3), the minimum 7-day compressive strength requirement is 175 kg/cm².

questions.q: 377. Humidity causes ……… of cement in bag .
questions.explain: Moisture in humid air can react with cement stored in bags, initiating premature hydration/setting reactions that spoil the cement before use.

questions.q: 381. Slump test is done for
questions.explain: The slump test is a standard field test specifically used to measure the workability/consistency of fresh concrete.

questions.q: 387. As compared to ordinary Portland cement, use of pozzuloanic cement :
questions.explain: Pozzolanic cement, through its secondary pozzolanic reaction with calcium hydroxide, results in improved long-term strength compared with ordinary Portland cement.

questions.q: 391. Expansive cement expands mostly during its :
questions.explain: Expansive cement is engineered so that most of its expansion occurs during the final hardening period, after initial set, to compensate for later drying shrinkage.

questions.q: 392. Soundness of the material means the resistance of the material against the effect of :
questions.explain: Soundness specifically refers to a material's ability to resist volume changes/deterioration from repeated cycles of freezing and thawing.

questions.q: 393. What is a graded aggregate ?
options: it has particles of all sizes
it has particles between 4 mm - 6 mm
it has particles between 10 mm - 15 mm
it has particles between 2 mm - 5 mm
questions.explain: A graded aggregate is one containing a well-distributed range of particle sizes, from the largest down to the smallest, rather than being confined to a narrow size range.

questions.q: 394. Finer grinding of cement
options: affects only the early development of strength
questions.explain: Finer grinding increases the surface area available for hydration, which speeds up early reactions and therefore mainly boosts early-age strength development rather than the ultimate strength.

questions.q: 397. The percentage of voids in cement is approximately :
questions.explain: Loose cement powder typically contains approximately 40% voids by volume between its particles.

questions.q: 398. *The resistance of an aggregate to wear is known as :
questions.explain: Abrasion resistance specifically measures an aggregate's ability to withstand surface wearing action, distinct from crushing or impact resistance.

questions.q: 399. For the construction of cement concrete floor the maximum permissible sizes of aggregate is :
questions.explain: For thin concrete floor toppings/finishes, the maximum permissible aggregate size is limited to 10 mm to allow a smooth, well-finished surface.

questions.q: 401. Fineness of cement is measured in unit of :
questions.explain: Fineness of cement is expressed as specific surface area per unit mass (e.g., m²/kg), i.e., area/mass, since finer cement has more surface area per unit weight.

questions.q: 402. The cement-sad ratio used in the compressive strength test of cement as per the Indian Standard Specification is :
questions.explain: As per Indian Standard Specification, the compressive strength test of cement is performed using a standard mortar of cement-sand ratio 1:3.

questions.q: 403. The initial setting time of lime-pozzolana, is :
questions.explain: Lime-pozzolana mixtures set relatively slowly, with a specified minimum initial setting time of 120 minutes as per standard requirements.

questions.q: 404. The rocks which are formed due to cooling of magma at a considerable depth from earth's surface are called
questions.explain: Plutonic (intrusive) rocks form from magma that cools slowly at considerable depth below the earth's surface, producing coarse-grained crystalline rock.

questions.q: 405. Depending on the chemical composition and mechanical properties, iron may be classified as
questions.explain: Based on carbon content and resulting mechanical properties, iron/iron alloys are broadly classified into cast iron, wrought iron, and steel — covering all the listed types.

questions.q: 1. The cement becomes useless if it absorbed moisture more than
questions.explain: When cement absorbs moisture beyond about 5%, hydration begins prematurely inside the bag, forming lumps and losing its binding strength, making it unfit for use.

questions.q: 13. The function of aggregates in concrete is to serve as
questions.explain: Aggregates act mainly as filler material, providing bulk and volume to the concrete, while cement paste acts as the binder holding them together.

questions.q: 16. In the manufacture of cement, the dry or wet mixture of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt at a temperature between
questions.explain: In the kiln, the raw mixture of calcareous (limestone) and argillaceous (clay) materials is burnt at very high temperatures of about 1500°C to 1600°C to form clinker.

questions.q: 17. The chemical ingredient of cement which provides quick setting property to the cement is
questions.explain: Alumina in cement lowers the clinkering temperature and imparts quick setting properties, though excess alumina can weaken the cement.

questions.q: 18. The gypsum is added to the cement for
options: providing high strength to the cement
controlling the initial setting time of cement
lowering the initial setting time of cement
questions.explain: Gypsum is added during grinding of clinker specifically to retard/control the initial setting time of cement, preventing flash setting caused by tricalcium aluminate.

questions.q: 19. Which of the following ingredient of cement when added in excess quantity, caused the cement to set slowly?
questions.explain: Excess silica in cement makes the cement set slowly, as it increases the proportion of dicalcium silicate which hydrates and hardens slowly.

questions.q: 20. Lime when added in excess quantity
options: caused the cement to expand and disintegrate
lowers the clinkering temperature of cement
questions.explain: Excess free lime in cement remains uncombined, and upon hydration it expands, causing the cement to become unsound and disintegrate.

questions.q: 21. After the final grinding, the cement is sieved thought IS sieve number
questions.explain: IS sieve No. 9 (90 micron) is used to check the fineness of finely ground cement after the grinding process is complete.

questions.q: 22. Efflorescence in cement is caused due to the excess of
questions.explain: Excess alkalies in cement react with moisture and carbon dioxide, migrating to the surface and crystallizing as a white efflorescence deposit.

questions.q: 23. The presence of tricalcium silicate in cement
options: offers high resistance to sulphate attack
questions.explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) hydrates and hardens rapidly, contributing to early strength gain, but it generates high heat of hydration and offers low sulphate resistance.

questions.q: 24. The presence of dicalcium silicate in cement
options: has more resistance to sulphate attack
questions.explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly, generates less heat of hydration, and provides better resistance to sulphate attack, so all three statements apply.

questions.q: 25. The tricalcium aluminate in cement has the property of
options: generating large amount of heat hydration
questions.explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts very fast with water, is chiefly responsible for the initial set, and releases a large amount of heat of hydration.

questions.q: 26. The C4AF in cement has the cementing value
questions.explain: Tetracalcium aluminoferrite (C4AF) contributes little to strength and has a poor cementing value compared to the silicate compounds.

questions.q: 27. High percentage of tricalcium silicate and low percentage of dicalcium silicate in cement results in
questions.explain: A higher proportion of fast-hydrating C3S relative to slow-hydrating C2S leads to rapid hardening, high early strength, and higher heat of hydration, all together.

questions.q: 28. The sum of the percentage of tricalcium silicate and dicalcium silicate for Portland cement varies from
questions.explain: The two calcium silicate compounds (C3S and C2S) together typically make up about 70% to 80% of ordinary Portland cement's composition, as they are the primary strength-giving compounds.

questions.q: 29. The cement, widely used in retaining walls, is
questions.explain: Retaining walls are mass concrete structures where controlling heat of hydration to avoid thermal cracking is important, so low heat cement is preferred.

questions.q: 30. Which of the following cements is expected to have the highest compressive strength after 3 days?
questions.explain: High alumina cement gains strength extremely rapidly, achieving very high compressive strength within the first few days, higher than other cement types.

questions.q: 31. In the manufacture of pozzolana cement, the amount of pozzolana material added to ordinary Portland cement clinkers is about
questions.explain: Portland pozzolana cement is manufactured by blending about 30% pozzolanic material with ordinary Portland cement clinker.

questions.q: 32. The hardening is the phenomenon by virtue of which
options: the cement does not undergo large change in volume when treated with water
the plastic cement paste changes into hard mass
the cement paste sets and develops strength
questions.explain: Hardening refers to the process where the cement paste, after setting, continues to gain strength over time through ongoing hydration.

questions.q: 33. The phenomenon by virtue of which the cement does not undergo large change in volume when treated with water, is known as
questions.explain: Soundness refers to cement's ability to not undergo excessive volume change (expansion) after setting when exposed to water, which prevents cracking.

questions.q: 34. The compressive strength of an ordinary Portland cement (1: 3 cement mortar cube) after 7 days test should not be less than
questions.explain: As per IS specifications, a 1:3 cement-sand mortar cube of ordinary Portland cement must achieve a minimum compressive strength of 17.5 N/mm² after 7 days.

questions.q: 35. The length of Vicat plunger in Vicat's apparatus varies from
questions.explain: The Vicat plunger used for the standard consistency test has a length specified between 40mm and 50mm as per standard apparatus dimensions.

questions.q: 36. The percentage of water for making a cement paste of normal consistency varies from
questions.explain: The standard consistency of cement paste, determined by the Vicat apparatus, is typically achieved with water content in the range of about 35% to 50% by weight of cement.

questions.q: 37. To perform the initial setting time test, the water is added to the cement at the rate of .... by weight of cement
questions.explain: For the initial and final setting time tests, water is added at the rate of 0.85 times the water needed for standard consistency (P), i.e., 0.85P, as per IS code.

questions.q: 38. To perform the compressive strength test of cement, water is added at the rate of
questions.explain: For the compressive strength test of cement mortar, the water content used is (P/4 + 3%) of the combined weight of cement and sand, as specified by IS code, matching option c's form (P + 3% of water).

questions.q: 39. The cubes of cement prepared for compressive strength they should be kept at a temperature of ............ in an atmosphere of at least 90% relative humidity for 24 hours.
questions.explain: As per IS standards, cement cubes must be kept at a temperature of 27°C ± 2°C in an atmosphere of at least 90% relative humidity for 24 hours before demoulding.

questions.q: 40. For reinforced concrete, the aggregate used is
questions.explain: Reinforced concrete can use a combination of fine aggregate (sand) and coarse aggregate (gravel or crushed rock) depending on availability and required properties, so all of these are used.

questions.q: 42. The aggregate which pass through 75 mm IS sieve and entirely retain on 4.75 mm IS sieve is known as
questions.explain: Aggregate passing 75mm sieve but retained on 4.75mm sieve is classified as coarse aggregate as per standard aggregate size classification.

questions.q: 43. The maximum particle size of coarse aggregate is
questions.explain: By standard classification, coarse aggregate can have particle sizes up to a maximum of 75mm, beyond which it is termed cyclopean aggregate.

questions.q: 44. The aggregate which pass through 4.75 mm IS sieve and entirely retain on 75 micron IS sieve is called
questions.explain: Aggregate passing the 4.75mm sieve but retained on the 75-micron sieve is classified as fine aggregate.

questions.q: 45. The aggregates of ......shape have minimum voids.
questions.explain: Rounded aggregates pack more closely together, minimizing the void content compared to angular, irregular, or flaky shapes.

questions.q: 46. The aggregates of ...........shape have maximum voids
questions.explain: Angular aggregates have rough, irregular surfaces and sharp edges that interlock poorly, resulting in the maximum void content among common aggregate shapes.

questions.q: 47. The aggregate is said to be flaky when
options: its least dimension is three-fifth of its mean dimension
its least dimension is equal to its mean dimension
its length is equal to its mean dimension
its length is equal to 1.8 times its mean dimension
questions.explain: An aggregate particle is classified as flaky when its least (thickness) dimension is less than three-fifths (3/5) of its mean dimension.

questions.q: 48. Bulk specific gravity of an aggregate is defined as
options: the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, excluding the natural pores in the aggregate particles
the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, including the natural pores in the aggregate particles
the weight of aggregate required to fill a container of unit volume
the difference in weight of the aggregate in saturated surface dry condition and in moist condition
questions.explain: Bulk specific gravity is defined as the weight of oven-dry aggregate divided by its total (bulk) volume, which includes the natural pores within the particles.

questions.q: 49. The apparent specific gravity of an aggregate is defined as
options: the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, excluding the natural pores in the aggregate particles
the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, excluding the natural process in the aggregate particles
the weight of aggregate required to fill a container of unit volume
the difference in weight of the aggregate in saturated surface dry condition and in moist condition
questions.explain: Apparent specific gravity is the weight of oven-dry aggregate divided by its absolute (solid) volume, excluding the natural pores within the particles.

questions.q: 50. An aggregate which may contain some moisture in the pores but having dry surface is known as
questions.explain: Saturated surface dry (SSD) aggregate has its internal pores filled or partially filled with water, but its outer surface is dry, matching this description.

questions.q: 51. An aggregate having all the pores filled with water but having dry surface is called
questions.explain: This is precisely the definition of saturated surface dry (SSD) aggregate: pores fully saturated with water while the outer surface remains dry.

questions.q: 52. A moist aggregate is one
options: whose all the pores are filled with water and also having its surface wet
whose all the pores are filled with water but having its surface dry
which do not contain any moisture in the pores but having dry surface
which may contain some moisture in the pores but having dry surface
questions.explain: A moist aggregate has all its pores filled with water and additionally carries free water on its surface, making the surface wet.

questions.q: 53. The resistance of an aggregate to compressive forces is known as
questions.explain: The crushing value test measures the resistance of aggregate to crushing under a gradually applied compressive load.

questions.q: 54. The resistance of an aggregate to wear is known as
questions.explain: The abrasion value indicates the aggregate's resistance to surface wear caused by rubbing or grinding action, such as traffic wear on road surfaces.

questions.q: 55. The resistance of an aggregate to the effect of hydration of cement and weather is called
questions.explain: Soundness of an aggregate refers to its ability to resist volume changes due to weathering action, freezing-thawing, and chemical reactions such as those from cement hydration.

questions.q: 56. The ratio of the volume of moist sand to the volume of dry sand is known as
questions.explain: The bulking factor is the ratio of the volume of moist (bulked) sand to the volume of the same sand in dry condition, reflecting the increase in volume due to moisture films between particles.

questions.q: 59. The internal friction between the ingredients of concrete is minimized by
questions.explain: Internal friction in a concrete mix can be reduced through several means together: using coarser aggregates, adding more water for lubrication, and reducing surface area/texture of particles, hence all of these contribute.

questions.q: 63. The maximum quantity of aggregate per 50 kg of cement should not exceed
questions.explain: As per general guidelines, the total quantity of aggregate (fine plus coarse) used per 50kg bag of cement should not exceed about 450kg for good quality concrete.

questions.q: 65. For reinforced cement concrete lintels and slabs, the nominal size of coarse aggregate should not exceed
questions.explain: For thin reinforced sections like lintels and slabs, a smaller nominal aggregate size (15mm) is used to allow proper flow around closely spaced reinforcement.

questions.q: 66. The main requirement, which a ware-house should fulfill is that
options: its walls should be water proof masonry construction
it must have large number of windows
questions.explain: A cement warehouse must protect stored cement from moisture, requiring both water-proof walls and a leak-proof roof (options a and b together).

questions.q: 67. The term 'ware-house pack' means
options: pressure compaction of bags in lower layers
pressure exertion of bags on upper layers
questions.explain: 'Warehouse pack' refers to the phenomenon where cement bags stored in lower layers get compacted due to the pressure of bags stacked above them.

questions.q: 68. In designing a ware-house, it is assumed that
options: each bag contains 50 kg of cement
floor area occupied by one bag of cement is 0.3 m2
height of each cement bag containing 35 liters of cement is 0.18 m
questions.explain: Standard warehouse design assumptions include a 50kg bag weight, about 0.3m² floor area per bag, and about 0.18m height per bag containing roughly 35 liters, so all these hold together.

questions.q: 81. The most useless aggregate is, whose surface texture is
questions.explain: A glossy surface texture prevents good bonding between the aggregate and the cement paste, making it the least useful/desirable aggregate surface type.

questions.q: 82. The bulk density of aggregates depends upon its
questions.explain: Bulk density of aggregates is influenced together by particle shape, grading (size distribution), and the degree of compaction achieved during placement.

questions.q: 84. The workability of concrete can be improved by
questions.explain: Increasing the cement content adds more paste to lubricate and coat the aggregate particles, thereby improving workability of the concrete mix.

questions.q: 95. Separation of coarse aggregates from mortar during transportation, is known,
questions.explain: Segregation is defined as the separation of coarse aggregate from the mortar matrix, typically occurring due to excessive vibration or poor handling during transport.

questions.q: 96. Separation of water or water sand cement from a freshly concrete, is known
questions.explain: Bleeding is the phenomenon where mixing water (sometimes carrying fine cement particles) rises to the surface of freshly placed concrete due to settlement of solids.

questions.q: 97. The maximum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is that of
questions.explain: Lime (calcium oxide) is the predominant chemical constituent of ordinary Portland cement, making up the largest percentage by weight among the ingredients listed.

questions.q: 98. Pick up the correct proportions of chemical ingredients of cement
questions.explain: In ordinary Portland cement, the typical approximate composition by percentage follows the order Lime : Silica : Alumina : Iron oxide as 63 : 22 : 6 : 3.

questions.q: 99. Efflorescence in cement is caused due to an excess of
questions.explain: Excess alkalis in cement react with atmospheric moisture and carbon dioxide, migrating to the concrete surface and depositing as a visible white efflorescence.

questions.q: 100. Di-calcium silicate (C2S)
options: provides less ultimate strength to cement
has less resistance to soleplate attack
questions.explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly and, correspondingly, releases less heat of hydration compared to tricalcium silicate.

questions.q: 101. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: The degree of grinding of cement, is called fineness
The process of changing cement paste into hard mass, is known as setting of cement.
The phenomenon by virtue to which cements does not allow transmission of sound, is known as soundness of cement.
The heat generated during chemical reaction of cement with water, is known as neat of hydration.
questions.explain: This statement is incorrect: soundness of cement actually refers to its ability to resist volume expansion/change after setting, not to sound transmission — the two share a similar-sounding name but different meanings.

questions.q: 102. For road pavements, the cement generally used, is
questions.explain: Low heat cement is generally preferred for road pavements as it reduces the risk of thermal cracking in these large exposed concrete surfaces.

questions.q: 103. You are asked to construct a massive dam, the type of cement you will use, is
questions.explain: Massive structures like dams require low heat cement to minimize the heat of hydration and prevent thermal cracking in the large concrete mass.

questions.q: 105. The diameter of the Vicat plunger is 10 mm and its length varies from
questions.explain: The Vicat plunger, used for measuring standard consistency, has a diameter of 10mm with its length specified to be between 40mm and 50mm.

questions.q: 106. Inert material of a cement concrete mix, is
questions.explain: Aggregate serves as the chemically inert filler material in a concrete mix, while cement and water are the active binding agents that react with each other.

questions.q: 107. If aggregates completely pass through a sieve of size 75 mm and are retained on sieve of size 60 mm, the particular aggregate will be flaky is its minimum dimension is less than
questions.explain: The mean dimension is the average of the two sieve sizes (75+60)/2 = 67.5mm; the flakiness criterion (least dimension < 3/5 of mean) gives 0.6 × 67.5 ≈ 40.5mm.

questions.q: 108. An aggregate is said to be flaky, if its least dimension is less than
questions.explain: By definition, an aggregate is classified as flaky when its least (thickness) dimension is less than 3/5 of its mean dimension.

questions.q: 109. Log angles machine is use to test the aggregate for
questions.explain: The Los Angeles abrasion machine tests the aggregate's resistance to abrasion and impact by tumbling it with steel balls, primarily measuring abrasion resistance.

questions.q: 110. If fineness modulus of sand is 2.5, it is graded as
questions.explain: A fineness modulus value of 2.5 falls in the range typically classified as fine sand, according to standard fineness modulus grading ranges.

questions.q: 111. A ordinary Portland cement when tested for its fineness, should not leave any residue on I.S. sieve No. 9, more than
questions.explain: As per IS specifications, ordinary Portland cement's residue retained on the 90-micron (IS sieve No. 9) sieve should not exceed 10% by weight.

questions.q: 112. According to Water- Cement Ratio law, the strength of workable plastic concrete
options: depends upon the amount of water used in the mix
does not depend upon the quality of cement mixed with aggregates
does not depend upon the quantity of cement mixed with aggregates
questions.explain: The water-cement ratio law states that, for fully compacted workable concrete, strength depends primarily on the water-cement ratio and not on the quantity of cement or aggregate, provided the mix is workable — reflecting all three statements together.
