questions.q: 117. Internal friction between the ingredients of concrete, is decreased by using
questions.explain: Adding more water lubricates the mix and using coarser aggregate (less surface area) both reduce internal friction between the ingredients, improving flow.

questions.q: 126. If the engineer-in-charge approves, the 10cm cubes may be used for the work test of concrete provided maximum nominal size of aggregate, does not exceed
questions.explain: Smaller 10cm cubes can be substituted for standard 15cm cubes only when the maximum nominal aggregate size does not exceed 20mm, to maintain a valid size ratio between specimen and aggregate.

questions.q: 128. For preparing ordinary concrete, the quantity of water used, is
options: 5 % by weight of aggregates plus 20% of weight of cement
10% by weight of aggregates plus 10% of weight of cement
5 % by weight of aggregates plus 30% of weight of cement
30 % by weight of aggregates plus 10% of weight of cement.
questions.explain: For ordinary concrete, a common rule of thumb for the required water quantity is 5% of the weight of aggregates plus 30% of the weight of cement.

questions.q: 134. The dimensions of a 35 liter forma for measuring aggregates by volume, are:
questions.explain: A standard 'farma' (gauge box) with dimensions of 27cm × 27cm × 48cm gives a volume of about 35 liters, used for volumetric batching of aggregates on site.

questions.q: 154. Workability of concrete for a given water content is good if the aggregates, are
questions.explain: Rounded aggregates have lower surface area and less interlocking friction, requiring less paste to coat them, resulting in better workability for a given water content.

questions.q: 155. On a grading curve, the gap grading is represented by
questions.explain: Gap grading, where certain intermediate particle sizes are missing from the aggregate mix, appears as a horizontal (flat) segment on a standard grading curve.

questions.q: 156. For the construction of cement concerted dams, the maximum permissible size of the aggregates, is
questions.explain: For general mass concrete dam construction, the maximum permissible nominal aggregate size is typically limited to about 40mm as per standard practice referenced here.

questions.q: 157. Setting time of cement can be increased by adding
questions.explain: Gypsum is specifically added during cement manufacturing to retard the fast reaction of tricalcium aluminate with water, thereby increasing (controlling) the setting time.

questions.q: 158. For soundness test of cement we use
questions.explain: The soundness test of cement can be conducted using the Le Chatelier apparatus (standard method); however, per the answer key, the Vicat apparatus is indicated here — noting that autoclave expansion is another accepted method, and this question's key specifies option a.

questions.q: 159. The most useless aggregate is one whose surface texture is
questions.explain: A glassy surface texture provides very poor mechanical bonding with cement paste, making it the least desirable and most 'useless' surface texture for aggregate.

questions.q: 162. The type of aggregates of same nominal size, which contain less voids when compacted, are
questions.explain: Rounded spherical aggregates pack together most efficiently for a given nominal size, leaving the least void space when compacted.

questions.q: 165. Bulking of sand is
options: mixing of different sizes of sand particles
questions.explain: Bulking of sand refers to the increase in volume of sand when moisture is added, caused by surface tension films of water separating the fine particles.

questions.q: 166. Slump test of concrete is a measure of its
questions.explain: The slump test measures the consistency (workability indicator) of fresh concrete by observing the amount of subsidence after the mould is removed.

questions.q: 167. For ensuring quality of concrete, use
questions.explain: Well-graded aggregates, containing a proper distribution of particle sizes, minimize void content and ensure denser, higher quality concrete.

questions.q: 168. The commonly used material in the manufacture of cement is
questions.explain: Limestone, providing the calcareous component, is the most commonly used raw material in the manufacture of Portland cement.

questions.q: 169. Ordinary Portland cement is manufactured from
questions.explain: As per the answer key, ordinary Portland cement's raw materials given here are gypsum and lime, gypsum being added to control setting time along with the limestone-derived lime compounds.

questions.q: 170. Workability of concrete is measured by
questions.explain: The slump test is the most common and standard method used to measure and express the workability of fresh concrete.

questions.q: 172. Le-Chatelier's apparatus is used for testing
questions.explain: The Le-Chatelier apparatus is specifically designed to test the soundness of cement by measuring its expansion characteristics.

questions.q: 174. Cement used for normal concrete construction, is obtained by burning a mixture of
questions.explain: Ordinary Portland cement is manufactured by burning a mixture containing siliceous, argillaceous, and calcareous raw materials together to form clinker.

questions.q: 175. The cement whose strength is a little lower than the ordinary cement during the first three months but attains afterwards the same strength, is known as
questions.explain: Low-heat Portland cement gains strength more slowly in the early months due to reduced C3S/C3A content, but eventually catches up to match the strength of ordinary cement.

questions.q: 176. For construction of structures in seawater, the cement generally preferred to, is
questions.explain: Portland-pozzolana cement offers better resistance to sulphate and chloride attack from seawater, making it the preferred choice for marine structures.

questions.q: 177. Vicat apparatus is used for
questions.explain: The Vicat apparatus is primarily used to determine the standard consistency of cement paste (it is also used for setting time, but per this question's answer key, consistency is indicated).

questions.q: 178. The cement becomes useless if its absorbed moisture content exceeds
questions.explain: When cement absorbs moisture beyond about 5%, premature hydration and lump formation occur, rendering the cement useless for construction.

questions.q: 179. The size of fine aggregated does not exceed
questions.explain: By standard classification, fine aggregate particles must pass through the 4.75mm IS sieve, so their size does not exceed 4.75mm.

questions.q: 181. Concrete gains strength due to
options: chemical reaction of cement with sans and coarse aggregates
questions.explain: The chemical hydration reaction between cement and water forms the cementitious gel that binds the aggregates together, which is the fundamental source of concrete's strength.

questions.q: 183. The quality of cement is tested by
questions.explain: Compressive strength testing of standard mortar cubes is the primary and most common method used to assess and certify the quality of cement.

questions.q: 185. Low heat cement is used in
questions.explain: Low heat cement is specifically used in thick/mass concrete structures, where controlling the heat of hydration is essential to prevent thermal cracking.

questions.q: 190. The diameter of needle used in Vicat's apparatus for the determination of initial setting time is prescribed as
questions.explain: The Vicat needle used specifically for the initial setting time test has a prescribed diameter of 1mm as per standard specifications.

questions.q: 191. In a cement store, the size of cement pile is 4 m × 3 m and its height is 1.8 m. The number of cement bags in the pile could be
questions.explain: Using standard warehouse assumptions (about 0.3m² floor area and 0.18m height per bag), the volume of the pile (4×3×1.8 = 21.6m³) accommodates approximately 400 bags of cement.

questions.q: 192. The heat of hydration of cement can be reduced by
options: Reducing proportions of C3A and C3S
Increasing the proportions of C3A and C3S
questions.explain: Since C3A and C3S are the compounds that generate the most heat during hydration, reducing their proportions in the cement composition lowers the overall heat of hydration.

questions.q: 194. Increase in fineness modulus of aggregate indicates
questions.explain: A higher fineness modulus value indicates that the aggregate contains a larger proportion of coarser particles, i.e., coarser grading.

questions.q: 196. Weight of an oven dry sand and air dry sand are 500 gm and 520 gm respectively. If the weight of the same sand under saturated but surface dry condition is 525 gm, then the water absorption of sand is
questions.explain: Water absorption is calculated based on the oven-dry weight: (525 - 500)/500 × 100 = 5%, comparing SSD weight to the oven-dry weight.

questions.q: 198. Soundness test of cement by Le-Chatelier's apparatus gives unsoundness due to
questions.explain: The standard Le-Chatelier apparatus test specifically detects unsoundness caused by free (uncombined) lime present in the cement.

questions.q: 200. For ordinary cement, the maximum expansion by Le Chatelier method should not be more than
questions.explain: As per IS specifications, the maximum permissible expansion for ordinary Portland cement measured by the Le-Chatelier method should not exceed 10mm.

questions.q: 203. For 1 bag of cement (50kg) the quantity of water required is
questions.explain: Using a typical water-cement ratio of about 0.7, the quantity of water required for one 50kg bag of cement works out to approximately 35kg.

questions.q: 209. Durability of cement concrete generally improves by
questions.explain: Increasing the cement content generally produces denser, less permeable concrete, which improves its overall durability.

questions.q: 212. The test conducted by Vicat's apparatus is for
questions.explain: The Vicat apparatus is primarily used to determine the standard consistency of cement paste (as well as setting times), matching option 'consistency' here.

questions.q: 213. The bulking of aggregate is due to
questions.explain: Bulking of fine aggregate (sand) occurs specifically due to the presence of moisture content, which creates surface tension films that push particles apart.

questions.q: 215. The maximum bulking of sand occurs at a moisture content of
questions.explain: Maximum bulking of sand typically occurs at a relatively low moisture content of around 5% to 8% by volume, before further water addition reduces bulking (as per the given key, 5%).

questions.q: 227. An aggregate which passes through 25mm I.S. sieve and is retained on 20mm sieve, is said to be flaky if its least dimension is less than
questions.explain: The mean dimension is (25+20)/2 = 22.5mm; applying the flakiness criterion (least dimension < 3/5 mean) gives 0.6 × 22.5 = 13.5mm.

questions.q: 229. The basic water demand depend on
questions.explain: The basic water demand of a concrete mix is influenced together by the quality (nature, absorption) of the materials used and the target water-cement ratio.

questions.q: 230. The sieve number used in the fineness modules test of cement is
questions.explain: Per the given answer key, sieve number 1 is used in the specified fineness modulus test procedure referenced in this question.

questions.q: 236. Slump test is done for
questions.explain: The slump test is a standard method specifically used to assess the consistency and workability of fresh concrete.

questions.q: 237. Vacat's apparatus is used to test the following property of concrete
questions.explain: The Vicat apparatus is used to determine the standard consistency of cement paste, which is a fundamental property tested before other cement tests are conducted.

questions.q: 239. The type of aggregates of same nominal size, which contain less voids when compacted, are
questions.explain: Rounded spherical aggregates of the same nominal size pack together most efficiently, leaving minimal void spaces when compacted.
